cards.title: Case Deletion for Identifying Unidentifiable Parameters
cards.claim: Specific unidentifiable parameters can be identified via a case deletion methodology: removing the column corresponding to a specific parameter from the Jacobian matrix and observing if the log|MF| vs log(σ²) relationship becomes continuous/linear (indicating the removed parameter was the source of unidentifiability).
conditions: Used when a model is determined to be unidentifiable.
Requires iterative assessment of individual parameters.
limitations: Computationally intensive for models with many parameters.
Relies on the assumption that removing the unidentifiable parameter restores identifiability for the remaining set.
cards.downstream_use: Use this diagnostic step to pinpoint which specific parameters (e.g., F in a one-compartment oral model) are causing structural unidentifiability, allowing for targeted model simplification or parameter fixing.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
